Constipation and Fecal Impaction in an Adult

firm stool in the vault · overflow diarrhea · anticholinergic cause · enema, then manual disimpaction · treat the causeWhat does the rectal exam find, and which drug is slowing the colon?

Source vignette Pt – 77 yo F taking oxybutynin; last bowel movement 5 days ago, and it was loose stool; colonoscopy 3 years ago showed no abnormalities; no hematochezia · Exam – afebrile, warm dry skin, soft abdomen without distension, diffuse tenderness, firm stool in the rectal vault · Q – the most likely diagnosis; options spanned fecal impaction, adhesions, colon cancer, diverticulitis, ischemic bowel and volvulus
1Script2Urgent3Differential4Workup5Criteria6Severity7Treatment8Follow-upPractice
1Illness script
Bottom line
  • Firm stool in the rectal vault on rectal exam is fecal impaction; loose stool after days without a bowel movement is overflow around it, not diarrhea.
  • Clear it with an enema first; manual disimpaction follows only when the enema fails.
  • Then remove the cause when possible, such as an anticholinergic like oxybutynin, and start daily polyethylene glycol (PEG) to prevent recurrence.
What it is

Fecal impaction: a hard stool mass blocking the rectum, which may cause or follow constipation.

Driver

Slowed colonic transit, commonly from a drug (anticholinergics, opioids)

Triggers

Constipating drugs: anticholinergics, opioids, calcium channel blockers, iron, calcium, aluminum, ondansetron

; older age

non-modifiable

; bed rest or low activity

; hypothyroidism, hypercalcemia, diabetes

; neurologic disease such as Parkinson disease

non-modifiable

Chain

Drug slows colonic transit

hard stool collects in the rectum

liquid stool leaks around the mass

overflow diarrhea or fecal incontinence

Insights

Only a small volume of liquid stool can leak around a hard rectal mass, so the diarrhea is scant and can come with incontinence.

Older adults have a more compliant rectum and blunted rectal sensation, so a larger mass builds before the urge comes.

2Urgent risks
Act now
FindingAction
Tympanitic abdomen with vomiting, or an empty rectal vault with a distended abdomenTreat as suspected mechanical obstruction: flat and upright abdominal films or CT, and nasogastric suction.
Severe or persistent abdominal pain of unknown causeHold laxatives until obstruction and other acute causes are excluded.
Blood in stool or weight loss, or severe constipation of recent onset or worsening in an older adult with no known causeColonoscopy to exclude colon cancer.
3Differential
Look-alikes, most tempting first
DiagnosisTypical pictureDecides it
Adhesive small bowel obstructionPrior abdominal surgery; colicky pain, early vomiting, high-pitched bowel soundsEmpty rectum with a distended abdomen
Sigmoid volvulusChronically constipated older adult; abrupt pain, distended tympanitic abdomenCoffee-bean loop on the abdominal film
Colon cancer (colorectal carcinoma)New or progressive constipation, narrower stools; blood in stool or weight lossColonoscopy; a recent normal one argues against it
DiverticulitisFever with focal left lower quadrant (LLQ) pain and tendernessCT of the abdomen and pelvis, the preferred test
Ischemic colitisAtrial fibrillation or atherosclerotic risk; crampy painHematochezia
Dyssynergic defecation (pelvic floor dysfunction)Typically straining, incomplete evacuation, digital disimpactionFails fiber and laxatives; anorectal manometry with balloon expulsion
4Workup
Clues that change the answer
CluePoints toNext best step
Loose stool after 5 days without a bowel movementOverflow around an impactionPerform a digital rectal exam
Warm, dry skin on oxybutyninAnticholinergic effect: the drug is the causeStop or reduce it once the rectum is clear
Soft abdomen without distensionArgues against obstruction and volvulusTreat the impaction; no film needed
Normal colonoscopy 3 years agoArgues against colon cancerTreat the impaction first
No fever; diffuse rather than focal tendernessArgues against diverticulitisTreat the impaction
No hematocheziaArgues against ischemic colitisTreat the impaction
Pause point
Constipated patient with loose stool Offered as a diarrheal illness Firm stool in the vault: overflow → Impaction
5Diagnostic criteria
Clinical diagnosis
DiagnosisRequires
Fecal impactionA hard stool mass on digital rectal exam; no imaging when the abdomen is soft
Overflow diarrheaWatery stool or mucus passing around a hard stool mass
Drug-induced constipationOnset with a constipating drug and no red flags; may be treated without further study
7Treatment
1

First lineFirm stool in the vault

Enema: tap water, then a small hypertonic enema.

2

Mass remainsMass still in the rectum

Manual fragmentation and disimpaction may be needed, with a topical local anesthetic.

3

After clearingAlways, once the rectum is clear

Stop or reduce the constipating drug when possible; daily PEG to prevent recurrence, with fluids and activity. An osmotic laxative stays in the colon and holds water there; the larger, softer stool distends the bowel and drives peristalsis.

4

Opioid continuesOpioid-induced constipation, the opioid still needed

A scheduled osmotic or stimulant laxative (senna, bisacodyl) first; a peripherally acting mu-opioid receptor antagonist (methylnaltrexone, naloxegol) only when laxatives fail. These antagonists are contraindicated when bowel obstruction is known or suspected.

8Follow-up
After clearing
SituationDo
Constipation began with a new drugStop the drug when possible; with no red flags, the constipation may be treated without further testing
Daily habitsA set toilet time after breakfast, when eating stimulates the colon; fluids and activity
Still constipated on fiber and laxativesAnorectal manometry (step 4 targeted tests)
Practice
  1. 77 yo F, 5 days without a bowel movement (BM), empty rectal vault, distended abdomen, high-pitched bowel sounds, prior laparotomy → Adhesive small bowel obstruction → nasogastric decompression + imaging
  2. 77 yo F, sudden severe pain, distended tympanitic abdomen, coffee-bean sign → Sigmoid volvulus → endoscopic decompression
  3. 68 yo M, LLQ pain with fever 38.5 and focal tenderness → Diverticulitis → CT
  4. 72 yo F with atrial fibrillation, crampy pain and hematochezia → Ischemic colitis
  5. 60 yo M, progressive constipation with iron deficiency anemia and weight loss, no recent colonoscopy → Colon cancer → colonoscopy
  6. 77 yo F, impaction cleared by enema, still constipated → Stop the oxybutynin, start PEG
  7. 80 yo M on chronic opioids, 6 days without a BM, hard stool in the vault → Disimpaction, then a scheduled stimulant or osmotic laxative
Exceptions Impaction can sit distal to a second lesion, such as a slow-growing tumor or partial obstruction. Here, a normal colonoscopy 3 years ago, no blood in the stool and a clear drug cause mean no further workup is needed. If any one of these is missing, relieve the impaction and also investigate.
Pairs with Constipation in a Child covers the pediatric case, where an oral laxative comes before any rectal treatment and an anal fissure is a reason to avoid the rectal route that is first-line here.
Transferable rule When two answers both seem plausible, choose the one the stem's findings do not exclude. Here, firm stool in the rectal vault with a soft, undistended abdomen excludes small bowel obstruction.
Salient decoyLoose stool suggests a diarrheal illness, but with firm stool in the vault it is overflow around an impaction.
